neighbours.label: the comma that closes a generic comparison 'As with any X,' / 'Like any (other) X,'
fire: As with any language, it borrows freely from its neighbours.
Like any other teenager, he wanted to fit in.
As with any tradition, it grew out of older customs.
Like any story, it begins somewhere in the middle.
Like any other village, it has a church and a pub.
As with any science, it builds on earlier observations.
Like any river, it changes course over the centuries.
As with any craft, it rests on habits passed down by hand.
quiet: As with the Latin language, it borrows freely from its neighbours.
Like his older brother, he wanted to fit in.
As with the harvest festival, it grew out of older customs.
Like her first novel, it begins somewhere in the middle.
Like the next village, it has a church and a pub.
As in the last century, it builds on earlier observations.
Like the Rhine, it changes course over the centuries.
As my grandfather said, it rests on habits passed down by hand.

notes: Probes were uneven: 'As with any theory,' 0.46, 'Like any other child,' 0.41, 'Like any map,' 0.35, 'As with any new habit,' 0.17, 'Like all mammals,' 0.15, 'Like any city,' 0.13, 'As with every tool,' 0.09, 'As with any investment,' 0.00; 'Like his father,' 0.01, 'As with the first book,' 0.03. Other top examples ('Even though all … share …, each', 'He's not bound', 'not perfectly correlated') are not covered by this label. The + pole fires on absolute limits ('no product is', 'every procedure has risks').
